title: Likely misreadings in a rubric
statement: Whether a rubric should list a question's likely misreadings, each checked on its own and answered when nothing else is met.
detail: The lesson engine's marking adapter for an animated version asks the judge about each misreading a rubric lists, as a question of its own, and reports one only when no criterion is met and none is unsure (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated-judge.js`). Every rubric the engine exports sets that list to empty (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated.js`), and its adapter for a 3D version has no misreading check at all.

evidence.quote: Common wrong turns → these should score 0. This is what makes the grader *discriminate*.
Proof — the real graded response (good answer → 2/2)
